newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse 1H turnover slightly up on 1H'96.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse 1H turnover slightly up on 1H'96.

text.p: The Montenegro Bourse on Monday reported a 7.14 percent rise in January-June turnover compared to the same six-month period last year.

Turnover in the first six months stood at 365.307 million dinars ($63 million) in 759 transactions, the bourse reported. Short-term securities accounted for 283.473 million dinars or 77.60 percent and giro money for 79.194 million dinars or 21.68 percent of total turnover.

In short-term securities, commercial paper accounted for 84.75 million dinars or 29.90 percent, National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) bonds for 77.30 million or 27.27 percent and other short-term financial papers for 121.42 million or 42.83 percent of total trade.
"Trade in short-term securities has been rising from month to month compared to the volume of giro money deals," a bourse source said.
Most of the discount and commercial paper was issued by the Montenegrin pension fund, the source said.
Long-term securities in the six-month period accounted for 2.64 million dinars or 0.72 percent of trade and involved primary sale of shares of Hipotekarna banka a.d. Podgorica.
In June, turnover fell to 54.59 million dinars in 165 deals from 88.65 million dinars in 126 transactions a month ago.
Short-term securities acounted for 38.45 million dinars in June, a drop on the 72.39 million dinars traded in May.
Giro money deals in June accounted for 16.14 million dinars remaining at almost the May level of 16.25 million.

There was no interest in Federal Republic of Yugoslavia 100 million dinars' worth of 30- and 60-day treasury bills which carried a 4.5 percent monthly interest rate issued on May 12 for federal budget needs.
Interest rates in May and June continued declining and averaged 10.5 percent per month in June.
"Interest rates have dropped. At the end of June most commercial paper was issued at nine percent monthly interest," the bourse source said.
According to the source, trading is expected to remain stable and at the same intensity over the summer months while interest rates are likely to decline further.
